History of Present Illness:
53-year-old woman. One day of severe epigastric pain radiating to the back with vomiting. She has known gallstones and no alcohol use.

Physical Examination:
Epigastric tenderness without focal inspiratory arrest at the right costal margin. Temperature 37.7 C; heart rate 94/min; BP 122/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 12.9 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 227 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 0.9 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 54 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 870 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 188 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 139 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 87 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.4 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: gallstones without gallbladder wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct 5 mm; pancreas partly obscured by bowel gas.
